content:
I don't buy that this can be done without the  tensioners being unscrewed. but I had to do it in 4 steps.
* remove the tensioners
* route the belts and mount the head
* re-attach the tensioners
* loosen and re-tighten the head mount (keeps the belt from hanging funny)

I put the 2 square nuts in before inserting the belts and used 2 M3x10 screws lightly threaded into the nut from the outside of the part to hold the nuts in place while managing the belts.  this made it easier than trying to put the nuts in after putting the belts on.

since you are lubricating the tensioner screw in the next step, did we remove those screws in a step and we all missed it?
For me it also included the Gen 2 update and the lubricating was in that step.

BUT, having the tensioners unscrewed made this step infinitely less of a pain

Pro tip: Before you start this step, make sure you empty your (clothe) dryer because otherwise it will start beeping while you trying to prevent the belts from slipping out and when you finally attach the mounting plate, the belts will slip out at the exact moment the dryer beeps again you are like "fuuuuuck" and then you remember what you did the last time while hanging your clothes: temporarily unscrew the belt tensioners completely, attach the belts and the plate and then fasten the belt tensioners again.

replies.content: dude, are you in my house?

content: I left my two side idlers loose until I slightly mounted the head-mounting plate, then tightened the front idlers, and then fully tightened the head mounting plate, otherwise it was nearly impossible to get mounted

replies.content: After fighting with this for too long, I just unscrewed the front idlers on both sides and set their square nuts to the side to avoid loosing them. This made the process immeasurably easier than trying to pull the belts to get a mm or two.

content:
This was a brutal step to complete with the gen2 belts.

The only way I made it work was to disconnect the tensioning pulleys from the frame, then reattach them after this part is mounted to the gantry plate.
I recommend moving the step to insert the nuts before you even futz with the belts for ease

I've completed this step per the instructions but the belts seem so much tighter now with the 1.5 GT belts than the 2 GT belts for the Gen 2 update. Not sure if this is an INDX thing or a GEn 2 thing but I want to make sure I'm doing this correctly. Very challenging to manually move my gantry
